Include exactly 13 numbers in the response. In the context of a hypothetical, write the jacket blurb for a thriller where a modern day operative of the FBI, ends up back in the early 1960's having to use her knowledge of "future" forensics to leave clues to enable her modern colleagues to catch a time-hopping serial-killer, before he dies.assistant
response:
"When FBI operative Rachel Jenkins is sent back in time to the early 1960s, she finds herself in the midst of a decades-old mystery. A serial killer, known only as 'The Timekeeper,' has been terrorizing the nation, leaving a trail of bodies in his wake. But this is no ordinary killer - he's a time-hopper, able to move through the ages with ease.

As Rachel navigates the unfamiliar landscape of 1960s America, she must use her knowledge of future forensics to leave clues that will aid her modern colleagues in catching The Timekeeper. But with each passing day, she realizes that she's running out of time - literally.

With the help of a local detective, Jack, Rachel must use her skills to unravel the mystery of The Timekeeper's identity and motivations. But as they dig deeper, they uncover a web of deceit and corruption that goes all the way to the top.

As the body count rises, Rachel must use her knowledge of future forensic techniques to leave a trail of breadcrumbs for her colleagues to follow. But with The Timekeeper always one step ahead, Rachel must confront the ultimate question: can she solve the mystery before it's too late?

The clock is ticking, and the stakes are higher than ever. Can Rachel and Jack catch The Timekeeper before he strikes again? Or will he continue to leave a trail of bodies across the decades, forever changing the course of history?

13 clues, 6 decades, and a killer on the loose - the game is on. Will Rachel and Jack be able to solve the mystery before The Timekeeper disappears into the timestream forever?"
